ranked.headline: Computational inference of microbial behavior from sequence and transcript data
ranked.summary: Recent publications apply sequence and transcript inference to microbiome substrate competition, plasmid copy number, and probiotic persistence.

ranked.headline: Graph and tensor methods resolve spatial heterogeneity in tissue and single-cell data
ranked.summary: Population-scale spatial omics and single-cell data demand consistent, interpretable computational frameworks.

ranked.headline: Learned models predict TCR, MHC, and antibody recognition with wet-lab validation
ranked.summary: Large MS-eluted peptide training sets and uncertainty-driven or continual learning loops are tightening the coupling between prediction models and wet-lab…

ranked.headline: Non-genetic B cell state stability accelerates antibody affinity maturation
ranked.summary: Recent computational work pairs germinal center models and lineage simulators with ground-truth benchmarking of B cell receptor inference methods.

ranked.headline: Fused encoders learn biomolecular representations for property and interaction prediction
ranked.summary: Recent work substitutes pretrained protein, chemical and text encoders and uses biological relationships as supervision.

ranked.headline: Auxiliary signals constrain biomedical image representations under distribution shift
ranked.summary: Recent preprints add auxiliary signals such as negative controls, organ priors, perturbation transcriptomics, and diffusion bridges to image models.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks expose uncertainty and integration choices in omics inference methods
ranked.summary: Sequencing and multi-omic tools are now assessed on ambiguity, inter-method agreement and metric choice rather than single-score ranking.

ranked.headline: Statistical methods quantify cell-level structure in spatial and single-cell omics
ranked.summary: Recent work adds calibrated inference and benchmarking to spatial and single-cell data across perturbation, ligand-receptor, and doublet analyses.

ranked.headline: Residue-level interaction inference from predicted and experimental protein structures
ranked.summary: Recent work applies AlphaFold3 and AlphaFold2 models and PDB-scale resources to interface, ligand, and cryptic-site analysis.

ranked.headline: Reference-quality genomes and pipelines extend comparative inference across lineages
ranked.summary: Pedigree-linked, multi-stage, and petabase-scale approaches now apply standardized genomic inference across disparate lineages.

ranked.headline: Structure-guided generative design of binders and peptides with predictive filters
ranked.summary: Structure-based predictors now steer closed-loop design of nanobodies and peptides, with experimental validation of candidates.

ranked.headline: LLM agents automate reproduction, ablation, and prioritization in biology workflows
ranked.summary: Agentic systems are now being applied across virtual cell modelling, variant interpretation, drug repurposing, binder design, and genomics benchmarking.

ranked.headline: Cross-species genome comparison resolves grapevine origins and Lupinus diploidization
ranked.summary: Expanded Vitaceae and Lupinus assemblies, plus multi-layer crop regulatory networks, now enable direct cross-species architecture comparison.

ranked.headline: LLM agents plan, search and refine protein sequence and biomedical ML pipelines
ranked.summary: Agentic LLM frameworks now close design loops using tools, reflection and inference-time search across protein and biomedical ML tasks.

ranked.headline: Out-of-distribution generalization limits ML and docking models for drug discovery data
ranked.summary: Benchmarks on DNA-encoded libraries, kinase bioactivity, and drug-blind cancer response show held-out performance depends on split design and dataset.

ranked.headline: Reproducible platforms formalize docking, workflow and single-cell data pipelines
ranked.summary: Recent preprints embed containerized execution, provenance tracking and standardized QC directly into domain analysis platforms.

ranked.headline: Cell-type-resolved fine-mapping and network models dissect genetic control of expression
ranked.summary: Joint single-cell eQTL fine-mapping and multivariate trait-level models now resolve variants to specific cell types and regulatory architecture.

ranked.headline: Reproducible workflows package sequencing analyses as rerunnable modular pipelines
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers across transcriptomics, metagenomics, and epigenomics release Snakemake and R workflows for reproducible analysis.

ranked.headline: Calibrating and extending variant effect predictors beyond missense substitutions
ranked.summary: Clinical calibration of indel predictors and tissue-resolved dosage metrics for structural variants extend interpretation beyond missense variants.

ranked.headline: Longitudinal and agentic benchmarks test automated biological sequence annotation
ranked.summary: Recent items benchmark LLM agents, protein function predictors and sequence ML platforms, exposing reproducibility and overinterpretation gaps.

ranked.headline: Physics-based and learned models predict binding, kinetics and selectivity
ranked.summary: Recent studies pair free-energy simulation, QM/MM and physically constrained meta-learning to predict selectivity, kinetics and membrane-embedded binding.

ranked.headline: Molecular feature representations drive predictive performance in drug-discovery models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a software release benchmark descriptor, graph, and geometric features as inputs for molecular property prediction.

ranked.headline: Genomic context shapes the design, evolution and 3D structure of regulatory DNA
ranked.summary: Context-aware models and high-throughput screens now probe regulatory DNA across 3D architecture, evolution, and design.

ranked.headline: Spatial models link cell arrangement and viral spread to immune activation readouts
ranked.summary: Spatial arrangement of dendritic cells, viral dispersal and interferon responses are now modelled together across scales.

ranked.headline: Deep learning fuses multi-omics and imaging data for prediction and cell-level inference
ranked.summary: Interpretable graph attention and pathway-informed networks are now applied across spatial, single-cell, and clinical omics data.

ranked.headline: Automated pipelines convert raw single-cell measurements into quantified cell-level data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers automate single-cell analysis across imaging, sequencing and proteomics, with some also covering acquisition.

ranked.headline: MD simulations map state-dependent conformational landscapes of Rac2, BRAF, and spike
ranked.summary: Dynamics-resolved models now distinguish functional states of Rac2, autoinhibited BRAF, and spike, beyond static structure alone.

ranked.headline: MD analysis choices govern fidelity of structural and energetic conclusions
ranked.summary: Recent MD analysis methods quantify how seeding, interface turnover, and selectivity-filter energetics shape structural conclusions.

ranked.headline: Model-guided perturbations nominate metabolic and cell-state therapeutic targets
ranked.summary: Model-based perturbation prediction is now nominating targets across organoid, glioma, and metabolic disease systems.

ranked.headline: Constraint and latent-space models infer metabolic fluxes and kinetic states
ranked.summary: Recent work recovers thermodynamically feasible fluxes and targeted kinetic dynamics without fully specifying network mechanics.

ranked.headline: Trajectory inference tools map pseudotime dynamics in single-cell and multi-omic data
ranked.summary: Recent tools add interpretable trend classification, transient-event detection, and reference mapping to pseudotime analyses of single-cell data.

ranked.headline: Copy number and platform artifacts expose limits of reference-based variant calling
ranked.summary: Phased assemblies, KIR genotyping, and a two-color dye artifact study expose errors in reference-based variant calling.

ranked.headline: Generative models steered by latent control and search for protein and RNA design
ranked.summary: Preprints now couple generative models with direct latent control of AF3 and OpenFold3 representations, plus geometric motif benchmarks.

ranked.headline: Models couple single-cell and spatial profiles to donor, species and tissue axes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers add donor-level, cross-species and subcellular resolution to single-cell and spatial profiling methods.

ranked.headline: Generalist segmentation models benchmarked on live microscopy and spatial-omics data
ranked.summary: Generalist segmentation models are now evaluated across live microscopy, CODEX, Xenium and volume EM rather than assumed to transfer.

ranked.headline: Minimal models link adhesion, division orientation, and tissue order to cell motion
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a phase-field study extend minimal, mechanistically explicit models of tissue flows, division orientation, and border cell migration.

ranked.headline: Inferring diffusion and transport parameters from stochastic trajectory and count data
ranked.summary: Trajectory-level stochastic models are being tested for when path data outperform counts and how to estimate diffusion and path-space divergences.

ranked.headline: Computational refinement of somatic variant and clonal inference in cancer sequencing
ranked.summary: Recent methods target accuracy of somatic structural variant calling and ctDNA methylation deconvolution, with reported gains in detection limits and F1 scores.

ranked.headline: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing benchmarks for detecting diverse RNA modifications
ranked.summary: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing is being benchmarked against rRNA and therapeutic RNA modifications, where AUROC alone proves insufficient as a metric.

ranked.headline: Verifiable FDR reporting and cross-software benchmarking in mass-spectrometry proteomics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints call for verifiable FDR reporting and uncertainty-aware quantification, paralleling reproducibility metrics in polygenic scoring.
